guide_line: Convert a reactant mass into a product mass.
steps: Change grams of the known substance to moles. Divide by its molar mass.
Multiply by the mole ratio from the coefficients: wanted over known.
Change moles of the product back to grams.

worked_example.q: Grams of H2O from 10.0 g H2 in 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O?

similar_problem.q: Grams of H2O from 16.0 g O2 in the same reaction?
similar_problem.hint: The ratio is 2 mol H2O per 1 mol O2.

problems.q: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O. Grams of H2O from 10.0 g H2?
problems.why: Grams to moles, times the coefficient ratio, then back to grams.
hints: Use the coefficient ratio. Do not assume 1 to 1.
